source.text: נָֽקְטָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֗י בְּחַ֫יָּ֥י אֶֽעֶזְבָ֣ה עָלַ֣י שִׂיחִ֑י אֲ֝דַבְּרָה֗ בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: Loathes my soul my life; I will let loose upon myself my complaint; I will speak in [the] bitterness of my soul.

en.L: My soul loathes my life; \q I will let loose my complaint upon myself; \q I will speak in [the] bitterness of my soul.
en.B: I am sick of my life; \q I will give free rein to my complaint; \q I will speak out of the bitterness of my soul.
en.R: I am tired of living. \q So I will not hold back my complaint. \q I will speak from the bitterness I feel inside.

es.L: Mi alma aborrece mi vida; \q daré rienda suelta a mi queja sobre mí; \q hablaré en [la] amargura de mi alma.
es.B: Estoy harto de mi vida; \q daré libre curso a mi queja; \q hablaré desde la amargura de mi alma.
es.R: Estoy cansado de vivir. \q Por eso no me guardaré mi queja. \q Hablaré desde la amargura que siento por dentro.

fr.L: Mon âme est dégoûtée de ma vie ; \q je laisserai libre cours à ma plainte sur moi ; \q je parlerai dans [l’]amertume de mon âme.
fr.B: Je suis las de ma vie ; \q je donnerai libre cours à ma plainte ; \q je parlerai dans l’amertume de mon âme.
fr.R: J’en ai assez de vivre. \q Alors je ne retiendrai pas ma plainte. \q Je parlerai de l’amertume que je ressens au fond de moi.

sw.L: Nafsi yangu imechukizwa na maisha yangu; \q nitaachilia malalamiko yangu juu yangu; \q nitasema katika uchungu wa nafsi yangu.
sw.B: Nimeyachoka maisha yangu; \q nitayaachia malalamiko yangu yatoke; \q nitasema kwa uchungu wa nafsi yangu.
sw.R: Nimechoka kuishi. \q Kwa hiyo sitazuia malalamiko yangu. \q Nitasema kutokana na uchungu nilio nao moyoni.

vi.L: Linh hồn tôi chán ghét mạng sống tôi; \q tôi sẽ buông lời than thở của tôi trên chính mình; \q tôi sẽ nói trong [sự] cay đắng của linh hồn tôi.
vi.B: Tôi chán ghét đời mình; \q tôi sẽ để mặc cho lời than thở tuôn ra; \q tôi sẽ nói lên từ nỗi cay đắng trong lòng.
vi.R: Tôi chán sống rồi. \q Vì vậy tôi sẽ không nén lời than thở nữa. \q Tôi sẽ nói ra nỗi cay đắng tôi mang trong lòng.

ko.L: 내 영혼이 내 생명을 싫어하니, \q 내 탄식을 내 위에 풀어놓고, \q 내 영혼의 쓰라림 속에서 말하겠다.
ko.B: 나는 내 삶이 지긋지긋하다. \q 내 탄식을 마음껏 쏟아 놓고, \q 내 영혼의 쓰라림에서 말하겠다.
ko.R: 나는 사는 것에 지쳤다. \q 그러니 내 불평을 참지 않겠다. \q 내 속에 쌓인 쓰라림을 털어놓겠다.

decisions.choice: my soul: I myself, my inner being
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the whole living self, with its desires and feelings. "My soul loathes" means "I loathe"; "the bitterness of my soul" is bitterness deep within.

decisions.choice: I will speak in the bitterness of my soul: Job repeats 7:11
decisions.reason: Job said nearly the same in 7:11, "I will complain in the bitterness of my soul." He comes back to his resolve not to keep silent, and in verse 2 turns to address God.

decisions.choice: let loose my complaint upon myself: give free course to my lament
decisions.reason: The verb ('azav) means to leave or let go. With "upon myself" it most likely means to let one's complaint run freely; some take it as "I will leave my complaint in my own charge". The sense in the verse is clear: Job will not hold back.

decisions.choice: I am sick of
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "I" for "my soul" (m1) in the first line, and keeps "soul" in the third, where "bitterness of my soul" reads naturally.

source.text: אֹמַ֣ר אֶל־אֱ֭לוֹהַּ אַל־תַּרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי הֽ֝וֹדִיעֵ֗נִי עַ֣ל מַה־תְּרִיבֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: I will say to God, Do not condemn me; make me know concerning what you contend with me.

en.L: I will say to God: Do not condemn me; \q let me know why {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} contend with me.
en.B: I will say to God: Do not condemn me; \q tell me what charges {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have against me.
en.R: I will say to God: Do not declare me guilty. \q Tell me why {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are bringing charges against me.

es.L: Diré a Dios: No me condenes; \q hazme saber por qué contiendes conmigo.
es.B: Diré a Dios: No me condenes; \q dime qué cargos tienes contra mí.
es.R: Le diré a Dios: No me declares culpable. \q Dime por qué me acusas.

fr.L: Je dirai à Dieu : Ne me condamne pas ; \q fais-moi savoir pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} plaides contre moi.
fr.B: Je dirai à Dieu : Ne me condamne pas ; \q dis-moi de quoi {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’accuses.
fr.R: Je dirai à Dieu : Ne me déclare pas coupable. \q Dis-moi pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} portes des accusations contre moi.

sw.L: Nitamwambia Mungu: Usinihukumu; \q nijulishe kwa nini unashindana nami.
sw.B: Nitamwambia Mungu: Usinihukumu kuwa na hatia; \q niambie una mashtaka gani dhidi yangu.
sw.R: Nitamwambia Mungu: Usiniite mwenye hatia. \q Niambie kwa nini unanishtaki.

vi.L: Tôi sẽ thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: Xin đừng kết án con; \q xin cho con biết vì sao Chúa tranh tụng với con.
vi.B: Tôi sẽ thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: Xin đừng kết tội con; \q xin cho con biết Chúa buộc tội con điều gì.
vi.R: Tôi sẽ thưa với Đức Chúa Trời: Xin đừng xử con là có tội. \q Xin cho con biết tại sao Chúa kiện con.

ko.L: 내가 하나님께 말하겠다. 저를 정죄하지 마십시오. \q 무엇 때문에 저와 다투시는지 저에게 알려 주십시오.
ko.B: 내가 하나님께 아뢰겠다. 저를 죄인이라 하지 마십시오. \q 무슨 일로 저를 고발하시는지 말씀해 주십시오.
ko.R: 나는 하나님께 이렇게 말씀드리겠다. 제가 죄가 있다고 판결하지 마십시오. \q 왜 저를 고소하시는지 알려 주십시오.

decisions.choice: I will say to God: Job's speech to God begins
decisions.reason: From here to the end of chapter 10, Job speaks to God. Since the speech runs to 10:22, every level introduces it with a colon rather than quotation marks.

decisions.choice: condemn me: declare me guilty
decisions.reason: The verb (rasha', causative) is the court word of 9:20 and 9:29: to pronounce someone guilty.

decisions.choice: contend with me: bring a case against me
decisions.reason: The verb (riv) is the lawsuit word of 9:3. Job asks God to state his charges, as an accused man has a right to know them (13:23).

decisions.choice: what charges you have against me
decisions.reason: Balanced says what contending means here (m3).

decisions.choice: "Tôi sẽ thưa ..." then "con" and "Chúa" to the end of chapter 10
decisions.reason: Job announces his words in the first person he uses of himself ("tôi", 10:1), then speaks to God as in 9:28-31: "Chúa" for "you" (a noun of address, with no deity_pronoun span) and "con" for himself.

decisions.choice: plain style for "I will say to God", then 합쇼체 with 주님 and 저 to the end of chapter 10
decisions.reason: The introduction is Job's resolve, said in his plain style (10:1); the words addressed to God take the prayer style of 9:28-31.

source.text: הֲט֤וֹב לְךָ֨׀כִּֽי־תַעֲשֹׁ֗ק כִּֽי־תִ֭מְאַס יְגִ֣יעַ כַּפֶּ֑יךָ וְעַל־עֲצַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים הוֹפָֽעְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Is it good to you that you oppress, that you reject [the] labor of your hands, and on [the] plan of wicked [ones] you shine?

en.L: Is it good to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} oppress, \q that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} reject [the] work of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands, \q and shine on [the] plans of [the] wicked?
en.B: Does it please {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to oppress me, \q to reject the work of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands, \q while {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} smile on the schemes of the wicked?
en.R: Does it make {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} glad to crush me, \q to throw away the person {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands, \q and to bless the plans of evil people?

es.L: ¿Es bueno para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} que oprimas, \q que deseches [la] obra de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos, \q y resplandezcas sobre [los] planes de [los] malvados?
es.B: ¿Te agrada oprimirme, \q desechar la obra de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} propias manos, \q mientras sonríes a los planes de los malvados?
es.R: ¿Te alegra aplastarme, \q tirar a la persona que hiciste con {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} propias manos, \q y bendecir los planes de la gente malvada?

fr.L: Est-ce bon pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} d’opprimer, \q de rejeter [l’]ouvrage de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains, \q et de luire sur [les] desseins des méchants ?
fr.B: Te plaît-il de m’opprimer, \q de rejeter l’œuvre de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} propres mains, \q tandis que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} souris aux projets des méchants ?
fr.R: Est-ce que cela {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fait plaisir de m’écraser, \q de jeter la personne que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as faite de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} propres mains, \q et de bénir les projets des méchants ?

sw.L: Je, ni vyema {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} kwamba unaonea, \q kwamba unaikataa kazi ya mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, \q na kuangaza juu ya mashauri ya waovu?
sw.B: Je, inakupendeza kunionea, \q kuikataa kazi ya mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} mwenyewe, \q huku ukiyatabasamia mashauri ya waovu?
sw.R: Je, unafurahi kuniponda, \q kumtupa mtu uliyemuumba kwa mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} mwenyewe, \q na kuibariki mipango ya watu waovu?

vi.L: Có phải là tốt cho Chúa khi Chúa áp bức, \q khi Chúa khinh bỏ công việc của tay Chúa, \q và chiếu sáng trên các mưu kế của kẻ ác?
vi.B: Chúa có vui gì khi áp bức con, \q khi khước từ công việc của chính tay Chúa, \q trong khi Chúa mỉm cười với mưu đồ của kẻ ác?
vi.R: Chúa vui khi đè bẹp con sao, \q khi vứt bỏ con người Chúa đã tự tay tạo nên, \q và ban phước cho kế hoạch của kẻ ác?

ko.L: 주님께서 학대하시고 \q 주님 손으로 수고하여 만드신 것을 버리시며, \q 악인들의 계획 위에 빛을 비추시는 것이 주님께 좋으십니까?
ko.B: 주님께서 저를 억누르시고 \q 주님 손으로 지으신 것을 내버리시면서 \q 악인들의 꾀에는 웃음을 지으시니, 그것이 주님께 기쁨이 됩니까?
ko.R: 주님께서는 저를 짓밟으시는 것이 기쁘십니까? \q 주님 손으로 직접 만드신 사람을 내던지시고 \q 악한 사람들의 계획에 복을 주시는 것이 즐거우십니까?

decisions.choice: the labor of your hands: Job himself, whom God made
decisions.reason: "The toil (yegia') of your hands" is what God has made with effort and care, that is, Job; verses 8-12 go on to describe how God formed him. It could also mean what Job has gained by his own toil, but "your hands" ties it to God.

decisions.choice: shine on: look with favor on
decisions.reason: God's face shining on someone is a picture of favor (Numbers 6:25; Psalm 80:4). Job charges that God favors the plans of the wicked while he crushes him.

decisions.choice: oppress: wrong, treat harshly
decisions.reason: The verb ('ashaq) is used of the powerful who exploit the weak (Leviticus 19:13; Ecclesiastes 4:1).

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one oppressed, Job, whom the verse means (m1).

decisions.choice: the person you made with your own hands
decisions.reason: Readable says who "the work of your hands" is (m1).

source.text: הַעֵינֵ֣י בָשָׂ֣ר לָ֑ךְ אִם־כִּרְא֖וֹת אֱנ֣וֹשׁ תִּרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Eyes of flesh [are] to you? Or as sees a mortal do you see?

en.L: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have eyes of flesh? \q Or do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see as a mortal sees?
en.B: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have human eyes? \q Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see things as a mortal sees them?
en.R: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have eyes like a human being? \q Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see only what people see?

es.L: ¿Tienes {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} ojos de carne? \q ¿O ves como ve un mortal?
es.B: ¿Tienes {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} ojos humanos? \q ¿Ves las cosas como las ve un mortal?
es.R: ¿Tienes {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} ojos como los de un ser humano? \q ¿Ves solamente lo que ve la gente?

fr.L: As-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} des yeux de chair ? \q Ou vois-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} comme voit un mortel ?
fr.B: As-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} des yeux humains ? \q Vois-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les choses comme un mortel les voit ?
fr.R: As-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} des yeux comme ceux d’un être humain ? \q Ne vois-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} que ce que voient les gens ?

sw.L: Je, una macho ya mwili? \q Au unaona kama aonavyo mwanadamu?
sw.B: Je, una macho ya kibinadamu? \q Je, unaona mambo kama mwanadamu ayaonavyo?
sw.R: Je, una macho kama ya binadamu? \q Je, unaona tu yale ambayo watu wanaona?

vi.L: Chúa có mắt xác thịt sao? \q Hay Chúa thấy như người phàm thấy sao?
vi.B: Chúa có đôi mắt của loài người sao? \q Chúa nhìn sự việc như người phàm nhìn sao?
vi.R: Chúa có mắt giống như con người sao? \q Chúa chỉ thấy những gì người ta thấy thôi sao?

ko.L: 주님께 육신의 눈이 있습니까? \q 아니면 사람이 보는 것처럼 주님께서 보십니까?
ko.B: 주님의 눈이 사람의 눈입니까? \q 주님께서도 인간이 보듯이 보십니까?
ko.R: 주님의 눈도 사람의 눈과 같습니까? \q 주님께서도 사람들이 보는 것만 보십니까?

decisions.choice: eyes of flesh: human, limited sight
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for what is human and weak. A human judge sees only the outside and must search for evidence; God sees the heart (1 Samuel 16:7). Job asks why God then acts as if he had to hunt for proof of sin (verse 6).

decisions.choice: questions expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: Verses 4-5 ask questions whose answer is plainly "no"; verses 6-7 draw the point: why then does God treat Job as a suspect?

decisions.choice: human eyes
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "flesh" stands for (m1).

source.text: הֲכִימֵ֣י אֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמֶ֑יךָ אִם־שְׁ֝נוֹתֶ֗יךָ כִּ֣ימֵי גָֽבֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Like [the] days of a mortal [are] your days, or your years like [the] days of a man,

en.L: Are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} days like [the] days of a mortal, \q or {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} years like [the] days of a man,
en.B: Are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} days like the days of a mortal, \q or {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} years like a human lifetime,
en.R: Is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} life short like ours? \q Are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} years as few as a person's years?

es.L: ¿Son {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} días como [los] días de un mortal, \q o {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} años como [los] días de un hombre,
es.B: ¿Son {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} días como los días de un mortal, \q o {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} años como la vida de un ser humano,
es.R: ¿Es {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vida corta como la nuestra? \q ¿Son {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} años tan pocos como los de una persona?

fr.L: Tes jours sont-ils comme [les] jours d’un mortel, \q ou {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} années comme [les] jours d’un homme,
fr.B: Tes jours sont-ils comme les jours d’un mortel, \q ou {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} années comme une vie humaine,
fr.R: Ta vie est-elle courte comme la nôtre ? \q Tes années sont-elles aussi peu nombreuses que celles d’un humain ?

sw.L: Je, siku {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} ni kama siku za mwanadamu, \q au miaka {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kama siku za mtu,
sw.B: Je, siku {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} ni kama siku za mwanadamu, \q au miaka {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kama maisha ya binadamu,
sw.R: Je, maisha {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni mafupi kama yetu? \q Je, miaka {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni michache kama miaka ya mtu?

vi.L: Những ngày của Chúa như những ngày của người phàm, \q hay những năm của Chúa như những ngày của loài người,
vi.B: Phải chăng ngày tháng của Chúa như ngày tháng của người phàm, \q hay năm tháng của Chúa như một đời người,
vi.R: Đời Chúa có ngắn ngủi như đời chúng con không? \q Năm tháng của Chúa có ít ỏi như năm tháng của một con người không?

ko.L: 주님의 날들이 인생의 날들과 같고, \q 주님의 해들이 사람의 날들과 같아서,
ko.B: 주님의 날이 인생의 날과 같고 \q 주님의 햇수가 사람의 한평생과 같아서,
ko.R: 주님의 삶도 우리처럼 짧습니까? \q 주님의 햇수도 사람의 햇수처럼 얼마 되지 않습니까?

decisions.choice: the question runs into verse 6
decisions.reason: The question of verse 5 is completed in verse 6: are God's days as short as a human life, that he must hurry to find Job's guilt? Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma; Readable makes it a question of its own.

decisions.choice: a man: a human being
decisions.reason: The word (gever) is a man in his strength; here, set beside "a mortal", it means any human being.

decisions.choice: Is your life short like ours?
alternatives: Are your days like the days of a mortal?
decisions.reason: Readable says what the comparison is about: a short lifetime.

source.text: כִּֽי־תְבַקֵּ֥שׁ לַעֲוֺנִ֑י וּ֭לְחַטָּאתִ֥י תִדְרֽוֹשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: that you seek for my iniquity, and for my sin you search?

en.L: that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} seek out my iniquity \q and search for my sin,
en.B: that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} must hunt for my guilt \q and search out my sin,
en.R: Is that why {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hunt for my wrongdoing \q and search for my sins,

es.L: para que busques mi iniquidad \q e indagues mi pecado,
es.B: que tengas que rastrear mi culpa \q y buscar mi pecado,
es.R: ¿Es por eso que andas buscando mis faltas \q y rastreando mis pecados,

fr.L: pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} recherches mon iniquité \q et enquêtes sur mon péché,
fr.B: pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} doives traquer ma faute \q et rechercher mon péché,
fr.R: Est-ce pour cela que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} cherches mes torts \q et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fouilles pour trouver mes péchés,

sw.L: hata ukatafute uovu wangu \q na kuichunguza dhambi yangu,
sw.B: hata ulazimike kuusaka uovu wangu \q na kuichunguza dhambi yangu,
sw.R: Je, ndiyo maana unayatafuta makosa yangu \q na kuzichunguza dhambi zangu,

vi.L: mà Chúa phải tìm tòi gian ác của con \q và tra xét tội lỗi con,
vi.B: đến nỗi Chúa phải lùng tìm lỗi lầm của con \q và dò xét tội lỗi con,
vi.R: Có phải vì thế mà Chúa săn lùng lỗi lầm của con \q và tìm kiếm tội lỗi của con,

ko.L: 주님께서 저의 죄악을 찾으시고 \q 저의 죄를 캐내십니까?
ko.B: 주님께서 제 허물을 뒤지시고 \q 제 죄를 샅샅이 찾으셔야 합니까?
ko.R: 그래서 주님께서는 제 잘못을 찾아내시고 \q 제 죄를 뒤지시는 것입니까?

decisions.choice: iniquity ... sin: two words for wrongdoing
decisions.reason: The two words ('avon, chatta't) are paired for wrongdoing and the guilt it brings (7:21; 13:23).

decisions.choice: that: the result God's short life would require
decisions.reason: If God were short-lived like a human, he might have to rush to find evidence. The "that" gives what Job sees God doing: searching him as an investigator searches a suspect.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 7
decisions.reason: Verse 7 completes this sentence ("although you know ..."), so every level ends with a comma.

decisions.choice: the question closes in verse 6, and verse 7 adds its "although" clause as a sentence of its own
decisions.reason: Korean puts the main verb last, so the Hebrew sentence that runs from verse 5 to verse 7 cannot keep each verse's words after its own marker unless the question ends here; verse 7 then follows as an added remark ("...데도 말입니다").

source.text: עַֽל־דַּ֭עְתְּךָ כִּי־לֹ֣א אֶרְשָׁ֑ע וְאֵ֖ין מִיָּדְךָ֣ מַצִּֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: Upon your knowledge that not I am guilty, and there is none from your hand delivering?

en.L: although {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that I am not guilty, \q and there is no one to deliver from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand?
en.B: although {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that I am not guilty, \q and that no one can rescue me from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand?
en.R: even though {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know I am not guilty, \q and no one can save me from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power?

es.L: aunque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} sabes que no soy culpable, \q y no hay quien libre de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano?
es.B: aunque sabes que no soy culpable, \q y que nadie me puede librar de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano?
es.R: aun sabiendo que no soy culpable, \q y que nadie me puede salvar de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} poder?

fr.L: bien que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} saches que je ne suis pas coupable, \q et qu’il n’y a personne pour délivrer de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main ?
fr.B: alors que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais que je ne suis pas coupable, \q et que nul ne peut me délivrer de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main ?
fr.R: alors que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais que je ne suis pas coupable, \q et que personne ne peut me sauver de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} puissance ?

sw.L: ingawa unajua kwamba sina hatia, \q wala hakuna aokoaye mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}?
sw.B: ingawa unajua kwamba sina hatia, \q na kwamba hakuna awezaye kuniokoa mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}?
sw.R: hata ingawa unajua sina hatia, \q na hakuna awezaye kuniokoa kutoka kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}?

vi.L: dù Chúa biết rằng con không có tội, \q và không ai giải cứu khỏi tay Chúa?
vi.B: dù Chúa biết con không có tội, \q và không ai có thể cứu con khỏi tay Chúa?
vi.R: dù Chúa biết con vô tội, \q và không ai cứu được con khỏi quyền năng của Chúa?

ko.L: 주님께서는 제가 죄가 없음을 아시고, \q 주님의 손에서 건질 자가 없는데도 말입니다.
ko.B: 주님께서는 제게 죄가 없다는 것을 아시고, \q 주님의 손에서 저를 건질 사람이 없다는 것도 아시지 않습니까?
ko.R: 주님께서는 제가 죄가 없다는 것을 아십니다. \q 그리고 주님의 힘에서 저를 구할 사람이 아무도 없습니다.

decisions.choice: upon your knowledge: although you know
decisions.reason: "Upon your knowledge" means "in spite of what you know" (compare 16:17, "although there is no violence in my hands").

decisions.choice: not guilty: not a wicked man
decisions.reason: The verb (rasha') is the court word again: Job claims God knows he is innocent of the charges.

decisions.choice: from your hand: from your power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power. Since no one can rescue from God's hand (Deuteronomy 32:39; Isaiah 43:13), God has no need to hurry.

decisions.choice: your power
decisions.reason: Readable says what the hand stands for (m3).

source.text: יָדֶ֣יךָ עִ֭צְּבוּנִי וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֑וּנִי יַ֥חַד סָ֝בִ֗יב וַֽתְּבַלְּעֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Your hands shaped me and made me together all around, and you swallow me.

en.L: Your hands shaped me and made me, \q together all around, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} swallow me up.
en.B: Your hands shaped me and made me; \q and now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn around and destroy me completely.
en.R: You shaped me and made me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands. \q Now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn and destroy me completely.

es.L: Tus manos me formaron y me hicieron, \q juntamente en derredor, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me devoras.
es.B: Tus manos me formaron y me hicieron; \q y ahora {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} das vuelta y me destruyes por completo.
es.R: Tú me formaste y me hiciste con {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} propias manos. \q Ahora {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} vuelves contra mí y me destruyes por completo.

fr.L: Tes mains m’ont façonné et m’ont fait, \q ensemble, tout autour, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’engloutis.
fr.B: Tes mains m’ont façonné et m’ont fait ; \q et maintenant {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} retournes et me détruis entièrement.
fr.R: Tu m’as façonné et fait de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} propres mains. \q Maintenant {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} retournes contre moi et me détruis complètement.

sw.L: Mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} iliniumba na kunifanya, \q pamoja pande zote, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} unanimeza.
sw.B: Mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} iliniumba na kunifanya; \q na sasa unageuka na kuniangamiza kabisa.
sw.R: Uliniumba na kunifanya kwa mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} mwenyewe. \q Sasa unageuka na kuniangamiza kabisa.

vi.L: Tay Chúa đã nắn nên con và làm ra con, \q cùng nhau chung quanh, và Chúa nuốt con đi.
vi.B: Tay Chúa đã nắn nên và tạo dựng con; \q và nay Chúa quay lại hủy diệt con hoàn toàn.
vi.R: Chúa đã tự tay nắn nên và tạo dựng con. \q Giờ đây Chúa quay lại hủy diệt con hoàn toàn.

ko.L: 주님의 손이 저를 빚으시고 만드셨는데, \q 사방으로 함께, 이제 주님께서 저를 삼키십니다.
ko.B: 주님의 손이 저를 빚어 만드셨는데, \q 이제는 돌아서서 저를 완전히 멸하십니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 직접 손으로 저를 빚어 만드셨습니다. \q 그런데 이제는 돌아서서 저를 완전히 없애려 하십니다.

decisions.choice: shaped me and made me: God as craftsman
decisions.reason: The first verb ('atsav) is to shape or fashion, as a potter or sculptor does. Verses 8-12 describe God's careful making of Job, to set against his destruction now.

decisions.choice: together all around: completely; or "afterward you turned"
alternatives: you made me altogether, all of me
decisions.reason: The words "together around" are hard to place. Read with the last verb, they mean that God destroys Job entirely, on every side. Read with the first, they say God made all of him. A slight change of the Hebrew gives "afterward you turned and swallowed me". All readings set God's making against his destroying.

decisions.choice: swallow me: destroy me
decisions.reason: To swallow up is to destroy completely, as in 2:3, where God says the Accuser incited him "to swallow him up" (to destroy him) without cause.

decisions.choice: now ... turn around
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the contrast between making and destroying, with "all around" as "turn around" and "completely" (m2).

source.text: זְכָר־נָ֭א כִּי־כַחֹ֣מֶר עֲשִׂיתָ֑נִי וְֽאֶל־עָפָ֥ר תְּשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember, please, that like clay you made me, and to dust will you return me?

en.L: Remember, please, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made me like clay; \q and will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} return me to dust?
en.B: Remember that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} molded me like clay; \q will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} now turn me back to dust?
en.R: Please remember that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made me from clay. \q Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} now turn me back into dust?

es.L: Acuérdate, te ruego, de que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me hiciste como barro; \q ¿y al polvo me harás volver?
es.B: Recuerda que me moldeaste como barro; \q ¿me harás volver ahora al polvo?
es.R: Por favor, recuerda que me hiciste de barro. \q ¿Vas a convertirme ahora otra vez en polvo?

fr.L: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, de grâce, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as fait comme l’argile ; \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me ferais retourner à la poussière ?
fr.B: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as modelé comme l’argile ; \q vas-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} maintenant me faire retourner à la poussière ?
fr.R: S’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as fait avec de l’argile. \q Vas-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} maintenant me changer de nouveau en poussière ?

sw.L: Kumbuka, tafadhali, kwamba uliniumba kama udongo wa mfinyanzi; \q {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} utanirudisha mavumbini?
sw.B: Kumbuka kwamba ulinifinyanga kama udongo; \q je, sasa utanirudisha mavumbini?
sw.R: Tafadhali kumbuka kwamba uliniumba kwa udongo. \q Je, sasa utanigeuza tena kuwa mavumbi?

vi.L: Xin Chúa hãy nhớ rằng Chúa đã làm nên con như đất sét; \q và Chúa sẽ cho con trở về bụi đất sao?
vi.B: Xin Chúa nhớ rằng Chúa đã nắn con như nắn đất sét; \q nay Chúa lại cho con trở về bụi đất sao?
vi.R: Xin Chúa nhớ rằng Chúa đã làm nên con từ đất sét. \q Nay Chúa lại biến con thành bụi đất sao?

ko.L: 부디 기억해 주십시오. 주님께서 저를 진흙처럼 만드셨는데, \q 저를 티끌로 되돌리시렵니까?
ko.B: 주님께서 저를 진흙처럼 빚으신 것을 기억해 주십시오. \q 이제 저를 다시 티끌로 돌아가게 하시렵니까?
ko.R: 주님께서 저를 흙으로 만드셨다는 것을 제발 기억해 주십시오. \q 이제 저를 다시 먼지로 돌려보내시렵니까?

decisions.choice: clay ... dust: the making and death of humankind
decisions.reason: God formed the first man from the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7) and said he would return to dust (Genesis 3:19). Clay is the potter's picture (33:6; Isaiah 64:7). Job asks whether God will undo his own careful work.

decisions.choice: will you return me to dust?: a question
alternatives: and you will return me to dust (statement)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read as a question or a statement; as a question it is a plea, which fits "remember, please".

source.text: הֲלֹ֣א כֶ֭חָלָב תַּתִּיכֵ֑נִי וְ֝כַגְּבִנָּ֗ה תַּקְפִּיאֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Did not like milk you pour me out, and like cheese curdle me?

en.L: Did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not pour me out like milk \q and curdle me like cheese?
en.B: Did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not pour me out like milk \q and let me thicken like cheese?
en.R: You formed me in my mother's womb, \q as milk is poured out and made into cheese.

es.L: ¿No me vertiste como leche \q y me cuajaste como queso?
es.B: ¿No me derramaste como leche \q y me dejaste espesar como queso?
es.R: Tú me formaste en el vientre de mi madre, \q como la leche que se vierte y se convierte en queso.

fr.L: Ne m’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas versé comme du lait \q et caillé comme du fromage ?
fr.B: Ne m’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas versé comme du lait \q et laissé prendre comme le fromage ?
fr.R: Tu m’as formé dans le ventre de ma mère, \q comme on verse le lait pour en faire du fromage.

sw.L: Je, hukunimimina kama maziwa \q na kunigandisha kama jibini?
sw.B: Je, hukunimimina kama maziwa \q na kuniacha niganda kama jibini?
sw.R: Uliniumba tumboni mwa mama yangu, \q kama maziwa yanavyomiminwa na kufanywa jibini.

vi.L: Chẳng phải Chúa đã đổ con ra như sữa \q và làm con đông lại như phó mát sao?
vi.B: Chẳng phải Chúa đã rót con ra như sữa \q và cho con đặc lại như phó mát sao?
vi.R: Chúa đã tạo nên con trong lòng mẹ, \q như sữa được rót ra và làm thành phó mát.

ko.L: 주님께서 저를 젖처럼 쏟으시고 \q 치즈처럼 엉기게 하지 않으셨습니까?
ko.B: 주님께서 저를 우유처럼 부으시고 \q 치즈처럼 굳게 하지 않으셨습니까?
ko.R: 주님께서는 저를 어머니의 태 속에서 만드셨습니다. \q 우유를 부어 치즈를 만들듯이 만드셨습니다.

decisions.choice: milk ... cheese: a picture of the forming of a child in the womb
decisions.reason: Job pictures his conception and growth before birth: as milk poured out sets into cheese, the seed became a body. Psalm 139:13-16 also describes God forming a person in the womb.

decisions.choice: You formed me in my mother's womb
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1), and turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: ע֣וֹר וּ֭בָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁ֑נִי וּֽבַעֲצָמ֥וֹת וְ֝גִידִ֗ים תְּסֹכְכֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Skin and flesh you clothed me with, and with bones and sinews you wove me.

en.L: With skin and flesh {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} clothed me, \q and with bones and sinews {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} knit me together.
en.B: You clothed me with skin and flesh \q and knit me together with bones and sinews.
en.R: You covered me with skin and flesh. \q You wove my bones and muscles together.

es.L: De piel y carne me vestiste, \q y con huesos y tendones me entretejiste.
es.B: Me vestiste de piel y carne \q y me entretejiste con huesos y tendones.
es.R: Me cubriste de piel y carne. \q Tejiste juntos mis huesos y músculos.

fr.L: De peau et de chair {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as revêtu, \q et d’os et de nerfs {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as tissé.
fr.B: Tu m’as revêtu de peau et de chair \q et tissé d’os et de nerfs.
fr.R: Tu m’as couvert de peau et de chair. \q Tu as tissé ensemble mes os et mes muscles.

sw.L: Kwa ngozi na nyama ulinivika, \q na kwa mifupa na mishipa ulinifuma pamoja.
sw.B: Ulinivika ngozi na nyama \q na kunifuma pamoja kwa mifupa na mishipa.
sw.R: Ulinifunika kwa ngozi na nyama. \q Uliifuma pamoja mifupa yangu na misuli yangu.

vi.L: Bằng da và thịt Chúa đã mặc cho con, \q và bằng xương và gân Chúa đã đan con lại.
vi.B: Chúa đã mặc cho con da và thịt, \q và đan kết con bằng xương và gân.
vi.R: Chúa đã bọc con bằng da và thịt. \q Chúa đã đan xương và bắp thịt con lại với nhau.

ko.L: 살갗과 살로 저를 입히시고, \q 뼈와 힘줄로 저를 짜 맞추셨습니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 살갗과 살로 저를 입히시고 \q 뼈와 힘줄로 저를 엮어 만드셨습니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 저를 살갗과 살로 덮으셨습니다. \q 제 뼈와 근육을 함께 엮으셨습니다.

decisions.choice: knit me together: weave
decisions.reason: The verb (sakhakh) means to weave or interlace. Psalm 139:13 uses the same picture of God forming a child in the womb.

decisions.choice: sinews: tendons
decisions.reason: The word (gid) is the cord that ties muscle to bone (40:17; Ezekiel 37:6, 8, where bones, sinews, flesh and skin come back together).

decisions.choice: muscles
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for the body's cords and muscle.

source.text: חַיִּ֣ים וָ֭חֶסֶד עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝פְקֻדָּתְךָ֗ שָֽׁמְרָ֥ה רוּחִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Life and steadfast love you have done with me, and your care has kept my spirit.

en.L: Life and steadfast love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have granted me, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} care has guarded my spirit.
en.B: You gave me life and showed me faithful love, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} care has watched over my spirit.
en.R: You gave me life and showed me faithful love. \q You took care of me and kept me alive.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal, faithful kindness
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the loyal love that keeps faith with someone, the love of a covenant (Exodus 34:6; Ruth 1:8). Job remembers that God once treated him with such love.

decisions.choice: care: watchful oversight
decisions.reason: The word (pequddah) is attention or oversight, a careful looking after. In 7:18 Job complained that God "visits" (the same root) him every morning to test him; here it is the care that kept him alive.

decisions.choice: my spirit: my breath, my life
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) is breath or spirit. Kept by God's care, it is the breath of life in Job (27:3; 33:4).

decisions.choice: kept me alive
decisions.reason: Readable says what keeping Job's spirit means (m3).

source.text: וְ֭אֵלֶּה צָפַ֣נְתָּ בִלְבָבֶ֑ךָ יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־זֹ֥את עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [things] you hid in your heart; I know that this [was] with you.

en.L: Yet these [things] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hid in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} heart; \q I know that this [was] with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: Yet all the while {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hid this in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} heart; \q I know that this was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} purpose.
en.R: But all along {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were hiding this plan. \q I know now that this is what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} intended.

decisions.choice: these things: what follows, God's hidden intent to hound Job
decisions.reason: "These things" most likely point forward to verses 14-17: while God was shaping Job with care, he was secretly planning to watch him and strike him. Some read it of the care just described, but the contrast "yet" fits the bitter turn.

decisions.choice: this was with you: this was your plan
decisions.reason: "With you" means "in your mind", "your intention" (23:14, "many such things are with him").

decisions.choice: this was your purpose
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the idiom (m2).

source.text: אִם־חָטָ֥אתִי וּשְׁמַרְתָּ֑נִי וּ֝מֵעֲוֺנִ֗י לֹ֣א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: If I sinned, then you would watch me, and from my iniquity not you would acquit me.

en.L: If I sinned, then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would watch me, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would not acquit me of my iniquity.
en.B: If I sinned, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would be watching me \q and would not let my guilt go unpunished.
en.R: If I did wrong, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would be watching. \q You would not let me go unpunished.

decisions.choice: watch me: keep me under guard
decisions.reason: The verb (shamar), "keep" or "guard", which in verse 12 meant God's protecting care, now means watching Job like a prisoner, waiting to catch him (13:27; 14:16).

decisions.choice: acquit: hold innocent
decisions.reason: The verb (naqah) is the same as in 9:28.

source.text: אִם־רָשַׁ֡עְתִּי אַלְלַ֬י לִ֗י וְ֭צָדַקְתִּי לֹא־אֶשָּׂ֣א רֹאשִׁ֑י שְׂבַ֥ע קָ֝ל֗וֹן וּרְאֵ֥ה עָנְיִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: If I am guilty, woe to me; and [if] I am in the right, not I lift my head, full of shame and see my affliction.

en.L: If I am guilty, woe to me! \q And [if] I am in the right, I cannot lift my head, \q being full of shame and seeing my affliction.
en.B: If I am guilty, woe to me! \q And if I am in the right, I still cannot lift up my head, \q for I am filled with shame and see only my misery.
en.R: If I am guilty, I am in deep trouble. \q But even if I am innocent, I cannot hold my head up. \q I am full of shame, and my suffering is all I can see.

decisions.choice: lift my head: hold my head high, with confidence
decisions.reason: To lift the head is to stand with confidence and honor (Psalm 3:4; Judges 8:28). Even if innocent, Job is too shamed by his sufferings to do so.

decisions.choice: see my affliction: look on my misery; or "drenched in my affliction"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "and see" (re'eh), which may be a command ("see my affliction!") or describe Job as one who looks on his misery. Some read, with a change of one letter, "drenched" (rewe), which pairs well with "full of shame".

decisions.choice: full of shame: sated with disgrace
decisions.reason: The word for "full" (sava') means filled to the point of being sick of it.

decisions.choice: see only my misery (B), my suffering is all I can see (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the Hebrew "and see" (m2) and say what it means here: Job's affliction fills his view.

source.text: וְ֭יִגְאֶה כַּשַּׁ֣חַל תְּצוּדֵ֑נִי וְ֝תָשֹׁ֗ב תִּתְפַּלָּא־בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it lifts itself up, like a lion you hunt me, and again you show yourself wonderful against me.

en.L: And [if] it lifts itself up, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hunt me like a lion, \q and again {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} wonderful against me.
en.B: If I hold my head high, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hunt me like a lion \q and again show {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wondrous power against me.
en.R: If I stand up proudly, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hunt me down like a lion. \q Again and again {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} use {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} amazing power against me.

decisions.choice: it lifts itself up: my head, if I raise it
decisions.reason: The subject is most likely "my head" from verse 15: if Job dares to hold his head up, God hunts him.

decisions.choice: like a lion you hunt me: God as the hunting lion
alternatives: you hunt me as one hunts a lion
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that God hunts Job as a lion hunts prey, or that God hunts Job as a hunter hunts a lion. In the first God is the lion; Job uses such a picture of God in 16:9.

decisions.choice: show yourself wonderful: display your marvelous power, here against Job
decisions.reason: The verb (pala') is used of God's wonders (5:9; 9:10). Job says with bitter irony that God's wonders are now aimed at him.

decisions.choice: I hold my head high
decisions.reason: Balanced names what lifts itself up (m1).

source.text: תְּחַדֵּ֬שׁ עֵדֶ֨יךָ׀נֶגְדִּ֗י וְתֶ֣רֶב כַּֽ֭עַשְׂךָ עִמָּדִ֑י חֲלִיפ֖וֹת וְצָבָ֣א עִמִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: You renew your witnesses against me, and you increase your vexation with me; changes and a host [are] with me.

en.L: You renew {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} witnesses against me \q and increase {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger toward me; \q changes and a host [are] against me.
en.B: You bring new witnesses against me \q and increase {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger toward me; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} send wave after wave of troops against me.
en.R: You keep bringing new witnesses against me. \q You keep getting angrier with me. \q You attack me with army after army.

decisions.choice: your witnesses: Job's sufferings as evidence against him
decisions.reason: In Job's courtroom picture, his sufferings are the witnesses God brings to testify that he is guilty (16:8, "my leanness rises up against me").

decisions.choice: changes and a host: troops attacking in relays
decisions.reason: "Changes" (chalifot) are relays or reliefs, fresh units taking turns; with "a host" (tsava', an army) the two words most likely make one picture: wave after wave of soldiers. Job's troubles come at him like an army that keeps sending in fresh troops (19:12).

decisions.choice: vexation: anger, grief
decisions.reason: The word (ka'as) is provoked anger or vexation.

decisions.choice: wave after wave of troops (B), army after army (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the picture of the two words together (m2).

source.text: וְלָ֣מָּה מֵ֭רֶחֶם הֹצֵאתָ֑נִי אֶ֝גְוַ֗ע וְעַ֣יִן לֹא־תִרְאֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And why from [the] womb did you bring me out? I would have expired and an eye would not have seen me.

en.L: Why then did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring me out from [the] womb? \q I would have died, and no eye would have seen me.
en.B: Why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring me out of the womb? \q I wish I had died before any eye had seen me.
en.R: Why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} let me be born? \q I wish I had died before anyone saw me.

decisions.choice: why did you bring me out of the womb: Job returns to his first lament
decisions.reason: Job asked in 3:11, "Why did I not die at birth?" Now he asks God directly why he let him be born.

decisions.choice: I would have expired: a wish that he had died
decisions.reason: The verbs after the question express what should have happened: Job wishes he had died at birth, before anyone saw him.

decisions.choice: I wish I had died
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the wish (m2) in plain English.

source.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־הָיִ֣יתִי אֶהְיֶ֑ה מִ֝בֶּ֗טֶן לַקֶּ֥בֶר אוּבָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: As [if] not I had been I would be; from [the] womb to [the] grave I would be carried.

en.L: I would be as though I had not been; \q from [the] womb I would have been carried to [the] grave.
en.B: I would be as if I had never existed, \q carried straight from the womb to the grave.
en.R: It would be as if I had never lived. \q I would have gone straight from my mother's womb to the grave.

decisions.choice: the grave: the burial place
decisions.reason: The word (qever) is a tomb or grave, the place of burial, not the word for the realm of the dead.

decisions.choice: as though I had not been: as if I had never existed
decisions.reason: Job wishes for a life so short it would be as though it never happened (3:16).

source.text: הֲלֹא־מְעַ֣ט יָמַ֣י וַחֲדָ֑ל וְשִׁ֥ית מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְאַבְלִ֥יגָה מְּעָֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: Not few [are] my days? And cease, and set from me, so I may be cheerful a little,

en.L: Are not my days few? Cease, \q and turn away from me, that I may be cheerful a little,
en.B: Are not my days few? Then stop! \q Leave me alone, so I can have a little cheer,
en.R: I have only a few days left. So stop! \q Leave me alone, so I can have a little joy,

decisions.choice: cease ... set: commands to God, the reading of the margin (qere)
alternatives: let him cease ... let him set (the written text)
decisions.reason: The written text has "let him cease, let him set" (yechdal, yashit), as if Job spoke of God or of his days. The margin tells the reader to read commands, "cease ... set" (chadal, shit), addressed to God, which fits the rest of the speech. The sense is the same: Job asks God to leave him alone.

decisions.choice: set from me: turn away from me, leave me alone
decisions.reason: "Set (yourself) away from me" means to let him be; Job asked God in 7:16 and 7:19 to leave him alone and look away from him.

decisions.choice: be cheerful: brighten up
decisions.reason: The verb (balag) is the one of 9:27: to brighten, to smile again.

decisions.choice: are not my days few?: my life is short
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes: Job's life is nearly over (14:1).

decisions.choice: I have only a few days left
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies (m4).

source.text: בְּטֶ֣רֶם אֵ֭לֵךְ וְלֹ֣א אָשׁ֑וּב אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: before I go, and not I return, to [the] land of darkness and deep darkness,

en.L: before I go, and do not return, \q to [the] land of darkness and deep darkness,
en.B: before I go to the place from which I will not return, \q to the land of darkness and deep shadow,
en.R: before I go away and never come back, \q to the land of darkness and gloom,

decisions.choice: deep darkness: thick, total darkness
decisions.reason: The word (tsalmavet) was long read as "shadow of death", as if made of the words "shadow" and "death"; it is better understood as a word for deep or thick darkness (3:5; 12:22; Psalm 23:4). Here it is the darkness of the place of the dead.

decisions.choice: and not return: death is one way
decisions.reason: Job has said the dead do not return (7:9-10; 16:22).

decisions.choice: deep shadow
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the sense of the word (m1) rather than the older "shadow of death".

source.text: אֶ֤רֶץ עֵיפָ֨תָה׀כְּמ֥וֹ אֹ֗פֶל צַ֭לְמָוֶת וְלֹ֥א סְדָרִ֗ים וַתֹּ֥פַע כְּמוֹ־אֹֽפֶל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: a land of gloom like darkness, deep darkness, and no order, and it shines like darkness.

en.L: a land of gloom like darkness, \q of deep darkness and no order, \q where [even the] light is like darkness.
en.B: a land of gloom as dark as night, \q of deep shadow without any order, \q where even the light is like darkness.
en.R: a land as dark as night, \q a land of deep shadow and confusion, \q where even the light is dark.

decisions.choice: deep darkness: the same word as verse 21
decisions.reason: The word (tsalmavet) is repeated; see the decision on verse 21.

decisions.choice: no order: no arrangement, chaos
decisions.reason: The word (sedarim, found only here) means rows or ranks, ordered arrangement. The place of the dead has none of the order of creation, not even day and night.

decisions.choice: it shines like darkness: even its light is darkness
decisions.reason: "And it shines" (tofa') most likely means "and where it is light": what passes for light there is as dark as gloom. Chapter 10 ends Job's reply with the word for gloom; the next speaker, Zophar, begins in 11:1.

decisions.choice: where even the light
decisions.reason: All levels supply "where" and "light" to say what "it shines" refers to (m3); Literal brackets "even the".
